-- Labels a user can put on projects to group them: a reusable tag (a name) and a many-to-many join
-- from projects to tags. A tag is created once and can label any number of projects; a project can
-- carry any number of tags. Both tables use IDENTITY ids like client, project, task and contact, so
-- the DB assigns them on insert while the seed path can still supply explicit ids (GENERATED BY
-- DEFAULT). A project_tag row is one (project, tag) pairing; UNIQUE keeps a tag from being applied
-- to the same project twice.
CREATE TABLE tag (
    id   BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE project_tag (
    id         BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES project(id),
    tag_id     BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES tag(id),
    UNIQUE (project_id, tag_id)
);

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The agent's test loop (DESIGN.md §15): build, start the whole app, run ONLY the specs currently
# present in e2e/specs (the agent sees only its own checkpoint's spec — blind), then stop.
# PINNED — do not edit. Contract: BASE_CHECKLIST.md §C, §D.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

## Summary

I added the ability to put labels (tags) on projects to group them, as a full-stack additive change.

**Database** (`src/main/resources/db/migration/V17__project_tags.sql`)
- New `tag` table (reusable labels) and `project_tag` join table (many-to-many, `UNIQUE(project_id, tag_id)`), both with `GENERATED BY DEFAULT` IDENTITY ids so seeds can supply explicit ids.

**Server** (OfficeFloor REST + Spring beans, all new files)
- Entities `Tag`, `ProjectTag`; repositories `TagRepository`, `ProjectTagRepository` (with `findByProjectIdAndTagId` / `existsByProjectIdAndTagId`).
- Views/body: `ProjectTagView` (pairing + resolved tag name), `ProjectTagRef` (request body).
- Logic + YAML wiring for four endpoints: `GET /api/tags`, `GET /api/project-tags`, `POST /api/project-tags` (add), `POST /api/project-tags/remove`. Adds/removes go through the `Audit` service (`PROJECT_TAGGED` / `PROJECT_UNTAGGED`).
- Extended `TestSupportController` to seed `tags` and `projectTags` and to truncate the two new tables on reset.

**Front-end** (additive, new files only)
- `features/projects/ProjectTagsPanel.tsx` — queries `['tags']` and `['projectTags']`, renders the chips (`project-tag-<id>`), a per-chip remove button (`project-tag-remove-<id>`), and a select of the not-yet-assigned tags (`project-tag-add`) with an add submit (`project-tag-add-submit`); mutations invalidate `['projectTags']`.
- `features/projects/projectTags.slot.tsx` — fills the existing `ProjectDetail` slot (order 30), so no existing page was edited.

The chip's `data-testid` sits on an inner `<span>` holding only the tag name so `toHaveText('urgent')` matches exactly, with the remove button as a sibling. `bin/e2e` passes and the frontend typechecks.
